summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Mitsubishi Electric is a ¥5.89 trillion Japanese electrical conglomerate whose relevance to AI data-center power sits in one segment — Infrastructure — and specifically in three product families: large static uninterruptible power supplies to 2 MW, power transformers to 765 kV, and gas-insulated switchgear and circuit breakers to 800 kV. That segment is where the company's growth now is: Infrastructure revenue rose 19% to ¥1,463.4bn in the year ended 2026-03-31 with operating profit up 73%, and Energy Systems orders rose 80% year on year in the quarter ended 2026-06-30 on what the company attributes to North American transformer business expansion. BACKGROUND. Founded 1921, listed in Tokyo (6503), roughly 150,000 employees across 200+ group companies. FY2026 (year ended 2026-03-31) revenue ¥5,894.7bn (+7%) and operating profit ¥433.1bn per company filings; net profit attributable to stockholders ¥407.8bn (+26%). The US arm is Mitsubishi Electric Power Products, Inc. (MEPPI), Warrendale, Pennsylvania, founded 1985 as a joint venture with Westinghouse Electric and wholly owned since 1989; its Critical Power Solutions Division in Pittsburgh has manufactured UPS since 1964 and is the entity that actually sells into data centers. Note the fiscal-year convention: the company labels the year ending 31 March 2026 as FY2026.
ecosystemRole: One of a small number of vendors that can supply the medium- and high-voltage equipment upstream of a data-center hall and the uninterruptible supply inside it from the same corporate parent — transformers, gas-insulated switchgear, vacuum circuit breakers and large static UPS. It is consistently named in the leading vendor set for data-center UPS, power transformers and gas-insulated switchgear by market-research firms, but no firm reachable in this research published a market-share percentage for it in any of those three markets, and where sources rank rather than list it falls below the top five in transformers. Its distinctive technical claim is vertical integration into its own power semiconductors, which underwrites both its silicon-carbide UPS line and its stated position against eco-mode.

productsAndServices.name: Large static UPS — 9900 Series
productsAndServices.description: Three-phase double-conversion uninterruptible power supplies from 80 kVA to 2 MW, built on three-level IGBT inverter topology and sold in the US through MEPPI's Critical Power Solutions Division. The 9900D is the range topper at 1200-2000 kVA, transformerless, modular in 400 kVA power modules and configurable N or N+1; the 9900CX is a 1050 kVA / 1000 kW unit parallelable to six; the 9900B covers 300-750 kVA; the 9900AEGIS covers 80-225 kVA and parallels to four modules.
highlights: Company describes the 9900B as the industry's first UPS with three-level IGBT topology; the 9900D is presented as the first 2 MW system to market and the smallest modular scalable static UPS at the highest power densities

Published double-conversion efficiency peaks at 97.0% on the 9900D and 9900CX and 96.6% on the 9900AEGIS; every published curve is for true online double conversion, and the company states plainly that no eco-mode is required
9900D and 9900CX are rated at unity output power factor (kVA = kW) at 1200-2000 kVA and 0.95 at 1050 kVA respectively; the 9900AEGIS is rated at 0.90
Company cites an Omdia 2025 UPS market research report for the claim that the 9900D is the best-selling UPS at 1500 kVA and above
Efficiency guarantee is backed by a stated refund of up to $10,000 per year for three years if a verified performance test fails to meet it
Self-load test function runs a burn-in at 20-100% of rating for 1-600 minutes at any power factor from zero to unity, removing the need for load banks
Battery options span VRLA, VLA, NiCad, pure lead and lithium-ion, with Narada, EnerSys, Deka/East Penn, C&D Technologies and Samsung SDI documentation published as 9900D peripherals
productsAndServices.positioning: Mitsubishi Electric names no competitor anywhere in its own UPS literature, benchmarking instead against ENERGY STAR and citing Omdia for share. Its stated differentiator is vertical integration: it says it is the only UPS brand that designs and manufactures its own semiconductors, and that competitors may incorporate older-generation Mitsubishi Electric IGBTs while only Mitsubishi Electric uses its current designs. Independent research places it in the leading data-center UPS vendor set alongside ABB, Eaton, Vertiv, Schneider Electric, Delta Electronics, Legrand and Piller Power Systems, without a published share figure.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct sales and direct field service through MEPPI's Critical Power Solutions and Service Center Divisions, with named field service technicians published individually; a MEPPI Alliance Program operates on the transmission and distribution side.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Corporate strategy published 2026-05-29 names development of next-generation 800 V and 1,500 V DC power supply systems and a PUE 1.1 data center as targets; MEPPI announced in October 2025 that it is developing 800 VDC power-delivery systems in collaboration with NVIDIA.

productsAndServices.name: SUMMIT Series silicon-carbide UPS
productsAndServices.description: A 500 and 750 kVA double-conversion UPS built on silicon-carbide devices in place of silicon IGBTs, rated at unity output power factor and published at 98.2% peak efficiency in true double conversion — the company's technical answer to eco-mode.
highlights: Published efficiency of 97.9 / 98.2 / 98.0 / 97.6% at 25 / 50 / 75 / 100% load on the 500 kVA unit, all in double conversion

The company's stated position is that silicon carbide makes eco-mode unnecessary: module efficiencies up to 98% are achievable without line-interactive operation, so there is no detection-and-transfer event to engineer around
ENERGY STAR rated, and the company says it sits at the top of all double-conversion UPS on the ENERGY STAR list
1.1:1 generator compatibility, active power-factor correction and harmonic mitigation, 65 or 100 kAIC options
500 kVA unit is 3,072 lb and rejects 42.0 kBTU/hr; the 750 kVA is 4,290 lb at 62.9 kBTU/hr
productsAndServices.positioning: Positioned against the industry's eco-mode trade-off rather than against a named vendor: where most large UPS buy back double-conversion losses by running the load on bypass during normal conditions, this line argues the losses were small enough to leave the load permanently on the inverter.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct through MEPPI Critical Power Solutions Division.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Silicon carbide is the stated bridge to the 800 VDC and 1,500 VDC systems named in the FY2031 strategy.

productsAndServices.name: Power transformers
productsAndServices.description: Core-form transformers from 69 to 275 kV and shell-form transformers from 115 to 765 kV, with the transition between the two designs at approximately 200 MVA bank capacity and a 275 kV high-voltage winding. The range includes generator step-up units, three-phase and single-phase autotransformers and gas-insulated transformers.
highlights: Company states it has supplied power transformers for over 95 years, with manufacturing beginning in 1910
Developed and manufactured a three-phase transformer for what it describes as the world's largest-capacity nuclear generator step-up application at 1,510 MVA

More than 550 shell-form special three-phase transformers whose transport size can be reduced to 50% of a conventional three-phase unit — a direct answer to the shipping constraint on large transformers
Gas-insulated transformers use SF6 as both cooling and insulating medium and are nonflammable, which is what allows them indoors or underground
Autotransformer reference installation named first-party: TEPCO Power Grid's Shin Kisaradzu substation
productsAndServices.positioning: Named among the top companies in the power transformer market by MarketsandMarkets alongside Hitachi Energy, GE, Siemens, Eaton and Hyundai Electric. Where independent sources rank rather than list, Mitsubishi Electric falls outside the top five, which are led by Siemens Energy and Hitachi Energy. No research firm reachable in this pass published a Mitsubishi Electric transformer share figure.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and through MEPPI in North America.
productsAndServices.roadmap: The company announced a transfer of its distribution transformer business in April 2024 and sold its Memphis, Tennessee high-voltage transformer plant to Hyosung Heavy Industries in 2019 for $46.5M, so the North American transformer position is not underpinned by a US plant. Collection gap: the company attributed Energy Systems growth in the quarter ended 2026-06-30 to North American transformer business expansion, and no source located in this research identifies where that capacity physically sits.

productsAndServices.name: Gas-insulated switchgear and high-voltage circuit breakers
productsAndServices.description: Gas-insulated switchgear from 145 kV to 550 kV and dead-tank gas-insulated circuit breakers from 72.5 kV to 800 kV with interrupting classes from 40 kA to 80 kA, plus air-insulated switchgear and medium-voltage gas-insulated circuit breakers.
highlights: GIS product matrix runs 145 kV / 3150 A / 40 kA at the entry point to 550 kV / 6300 A / 63 kA on the two-break 500MITS, with iso-phase enclosures above 245 kV

Company states its first GIS was built in 1968, its first 500 kV hybrid GIS substation in 1973, and the world's first 550 kV fully gas-insulated switchyard at Kansai Electric's Ohi Nuclear Power Station in 1976
Installed base stated as more than 20,000 GIS bays worldwide on the current product page, up from more than 10,000 in the archived brochure

High-voltage circuit breakers offer mixed SF6/CF4 gas for cold climates, operation from -30°C to +50°C and to -50°C with tank heaters, gang and independent-pole operation, and synchronous control on all IPO breakers
Company states its high-voltage circuit breakers are fully assembled and tested in the USA
productsAndServices.positioning: Named among the gas-insulated switchgear majors by Straits Research and Mordor Intelligence alongside ABB, Siemens Energy, Hitachi Energy, GE Vernova and Toshiba Energy Systems, with a second participant list adding Eaton, Powell Industries, Schneider Electric and Hyosung Heavy. No GIS share percentage for Mitsubishi Electric was found in any source.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and through MEPPI, with a MEPPI Alliance Program for qualifying customers.
productsAndServices.roadmap: SF6-free is the stated direction: a 72 kV vacuum circuit breaker with dry-air insulation is the current flagship, the company points to forthcoming vacuum models on its SF6-free journey, and it signed a memorandum of understanding with Siemens Energy in 2021 to study jointly developed zero-global-warming-potential high-voltage switching starting with a 245 kV dead-tank breaker.

productsAndServices.name: Medium-voltage vacuum circuit breakers
productsAndServices.description: Vacuum circuit breakers from 5 kV to 72 kV with three-cycle interrupting time, spanning 1200 A to 3000 A continuous and 25 kA to 31.5 kA short-circuit ratings, positioned as the SF6-free path for medium- and sub-transmission voltages.
highlights: 72 kV unit rated 31.5 kA and 2000 A with dry-air insulation — the company's SF6-free flagship at sub-transmission voltage
38 kV and 27 kV units operate from -50°C to +50°C, with the 27 kV rated to 3000 A continuous
Company states the breakers are M2 life-tested for 10,000 operations and use fully welded cabinets
Stated benefit is the absence of greenhouse gases entirely, rather than a lower-GWP substitute
Vacuum circuit breakers are the initial and transitioning product for the new Pennsylvania switchgear factory
productsAndServices.positioning: Profiled alongside Powell Industries, ABB, Siemens, Schneider Electric, Eaton, GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy and Toshiba International in Mordor Intelligence's North America medium-voltage switchgear roster, where the top five are said to control roughly 55-60% of the market. Mitsubishi Electric is not in that top five and no individual share is published. Metal-clad switchgear is not a named MEPPI product line.
productsAndServices.roadmap: The $86M Pennsylvania factory begins with vacuum and gas circuit breakers and transitions to predominantly vacuum circuit breakers.

productsAndServices.name: Data-center cooling and integrated power
productsAndServices.description: The CritiCool line of air-cooled chillers, a MEWALL thermal wall and wall-mounted direct-expansion units at 10, 20 and 40 kW, introduced in 2021 and sold alongside the UPS line as an integrated power-and-cooling offer for North American data centers.
highlights: Cooling was added to the UPS division's line in 2021, three years before the current AI data-center build cycle
Delivered through a strategic alliance between MEPPI's UPS division and Mitsubishi Electric Hydronics and IT Cooling Systems S.p.A. of Italy, announced April 2021
Positioned as turnkey power protection plus IT cooling from one supplier for North American data-center applications
The FY2031 corporate strategy names a PUE 1.1 data center as a development target, which is a cooling claim rather than a power one
productsAndServices.positioning: A cross-sell attached to the UPS franchise rather than a standalone thermal business; the company does not publish share or competitive positioning for it.
productsAndServices.roadmap: PUE 1.1 data center named as a development target in the FY2031 strategy.

productsAndServices.name: Grid software, DERMS and energy management
productsAndServices.description: A software layer over the transmission and distribution hardware business, assembled by acquisition: Smarter Grid Solutions for distributed energy resource management in 2021, and an agreement announced in August 2026 to wholly acquire PCI Energy Solutions of Norman, Oklahoma for approximately $1.4bn.
highlights: PCI Energy Solutions supplies energy-trading, scheduling and forecasting software to power-market participants; trade coverage reports its platform touches around 60% of US electricity generation
PCI is to become a wholly owned subsidiary with closing expected before the end of 2026, subject to regulatory approval
Smarter Grid Solutions, acquired in March 2021, brought distributed energy resource management; its integration with Clean Power Research was launched at DISTRIBUTECH 2025
Mitsubishi Electric also offers an SF6 gas monitoring and analytics system, a synchronous condenser, HVDC, FACTS/STATCOM and BESS on the same transmission and distribution catalogue
The ME Innovation Fund invested in Lucend, a US startup with an AI platform for data-center operational optimization, in January 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: The acquisition moves Mitsubishi Electric from selling grid hardware to selling the software that dispatches it, in the same direction Schneider Electric and Siemens have taken with EcoStruxure Grid and Xcelerator. It is the largest single capital commitment in the company's recent record and is a market-operations play rather than a data-center one.
targetSegments: Independent system operators and market participants
productsAndServices.roadmap: PCI closing expected before end-2026; the FY2031 strategy targets Solutions revenue of ¥1.0trn at a 15% operating margin, up from ¥0.4trn at 7%.

recentDevelopments.headline: Agreement signed to wholly acquire PCI Energy Solutions of Norman, Oklahoma for approximately US$1.4bn, closing expected before end-2026 subject to regulatory approval
recentDevelopments.read: The largest capital commitment in the company's recent record moves it from selling grid hardware to selling the market software that dispatches it — trade coverage puts PCI's platform in touch with around 60% of US electricity generation.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended 2026-06-30): revenue ¥1,497.1bn (+14.0%), adjusted operating profit ¥144.3bn (+53.8%); full-year guidance raised to ¥6,270.0bn revenue and ¥620.0bn adjusted operating profit
recentDevelopments.read: Energy Systems orders rose 80% year on year in the quarter and the company attributed segment growth to North American transformer business expansion — the clearest signal yet that the AI build cycle is reaching the transmission and distribution side of this company.

recentDevelopments.headline: New medium-term corporate strategy sets FY2031 targets: 12% adjusted operating margin excluding automotive, 12% ROE, 3-5% revenue CAGR, and development of next-generation 800 V and 1,500 V DC power supply systems plus a PUE 1.1 data center
recentDevelopments.read: The DC-architecture and PUE targets put data-center power in the corporate plan rather than only in a divisional catalogue, which is what makes the NVIDIA collaboration a strategy rather than a product line.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2026 (year ended 2026-03-31): record revenue ¥5,894.7bn (+7%) and operating profit ¥433.1bn; net profit attributable to stockholders ¥407.8bn (+26%); Infrastructure segment revenue ¥1,463.4bn (+19%) with operating profit up 73%
recentDevelopments.read: The growth is concentrated in the segment that carries UPS and transmission and distribution, and the record operating-profit headlines circulating in trade press are the ex-restructuring figure rather than the reported one.

recentDevelopments.headline: MEPPI relocates its California service center from Escondido to Vista, nearly doubling operational space, citing surging demand for critical power infrastructure
recentDevelopments.read: Service capacity is the constraint that shows up second in a critical-power business — an installed base grows before the field organization does, and this is the company acting on that.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q3 FY2026: revenue ¥1,423.5bn but reported operating profit ¥70.3bn, down ¥56.4bn year on year after ¥74.3bn of Next-Stage restructuring charges; full-year restructuring estimate raised from ¥40.0bn to ¥100.0bn and reported operating profit guidance cut ¥30.0bn
recentDevelopments.read: The gap between the ex-restructuring and reported lines is the year's single most misread number: guidance for ex-restructuring profit rose ¥30bn in the same breath that reported profit guidance fell ¥30bn.

recentDevelopments.headline: ME Innovation Fund invests in Lucend, a US startup with an AI platform for data-center operational optimization
recentDevelopments.read: A small cheque aimed at the layer above the hardware — pairing operational optimization software with the company's own power and cooling equipment.

recentDevelopments.headline: Next-generation gas turbine control system for thermal power plants completes functional testing, jointly developed by Mitsubishi Power and Mitsubishi Electric, with market launch targeted for fiscal 2026
recentDevelopments.read: The two Mitsubishi-named companies are legally and operationally separate, and this is the one place in the public record where they build a product together — control and instrumentation from the electrical company, the machine from the heavy-industry one.

recentDevelopments.headline: MEPPI announces it is developing 800 VDC power-delivery systems for next-generation AI factories through collaboration with NVIDIA
recentDevelopments.read: This is the company's entry into the rack-power architecture conversation, and it is visible only in a first-party release — independent coverage of NVIDIA's 800 VDC ecosystem names ABB, Hitachi Energy, Schneider Electric and Vertiv and does not name Mitsubishi Electric.

recentDevelopments.headline: MEPPI marks 40 years since its 1985 founding as WM Power Products, a 50/50 joint venture with Westinghouse Electric that became a wholly owned subsidiary in 1989
recentDevelopments.read: The US arm is older than the AI cycle by four decades, and its UPS manufacturing heritage runs to 1964 — relevant when a buyer is weighing service continuity over a twenty-year asset life.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2025 (year ended 2025-03-31): revenue ¥5,521.7bn and operating profit ¥391.8bn, both records; ¥100bn buyback completed with more than 29.8 million shares repurchased
recentDevelopments.read: The prior year's record set the base the FY2026 comparison runs against, and the buyback signals a balance sheet with room ahead of the PCI acquisition.

recentDevelopments.headline: MEPPI to build a 160,000 sq ft advanced switchgear factory in the Pittsburgh region for US$86M, initially producing vacuum and gas circuit breakers and transitioning to predominantly vacuum breakers, with more than 200 full-time jobs at capacity
recentDevelopments.read: Combined with a parallel Japanese investment the programme is about US$110M / ¥16bn, and it is squarely a tariff and lead-time hedge: domestic assembly of the product line whose imported equivalent now carries a Section 232 derivative duty.

recentDevelopments.headline: Mitsubishi Electric announces strengthened production facilities for its energy systems business in the US and Japan, supported by a US$4M Pennsylvania RACP grant and a US$2.75M Pennsylvania First grant
recentDevelopments.read: State money on a Japanese manufacturer's US switchgear plant is the same bargain being struck across the grid-equipment industry — public subsidy against domestic capacity for equipment the grid cannot get.

recentDevelopments.headline: Mitsubishi Electric announces the transfer of its distribution transformer business
recentDevelopments.read: Read alongside the 2019 sale of the Memphis high-voltage transformer plant, the company has been narrowing rather than broadening its North American transformer manufacturing footprint — which makes the Q1 FY2027 attribution of growth to North American transformer business the dossier's outstanding question.

recentDevelopments.headline: External investigative committee concludes its review of all 22 Japanese sites, reporting 197 cases of improper quality control across four reports
recentDevelopments.read: The company admitted falsifying transformer test data over roughly four decades, which is the single most consequential risk item for a dossier centred on transformers and switchgear; the president resigned in July 2021 and the chairman in October 2021.

recentDevelopments.headline: MEPPI acquires Computer Protection Technology, a southern California critical-power service provider
recentDevelopments.read: Buying field service rather than product — the recurring-revenue half of a critical-power franchise and the part a customer actually experiences.

recentDevelopments.headline: Mitsubishi Electric and Siemens Energy sign a memorandum of understanding on a feasibility study for jointly developed zero-global-warming-potential high-voltage switching, beginning with a 245 kV dead-tank circuit breaker
recentDevelopments.read: Two competitors in gas-insulated switchgear cooperating on the technology that would obsolete the gas both of them sell — a regulatory-risk hedge structured as a partnership.

recentDevelopments.headline: MEPPI's UPS division forms a strategic alliance with Mitsubishi Electric Hydronics and IT Cooling Systems (MEHITS) of Italy for turnkey power protection and IT cooling in North American data centers
recentDevelopments.read: Cooling was attached to the UPS franchise in 2021, three years before the current build cycle — the cross-sell predates the demand.

recentDevelopments.headline: MEPPI sells its Memphis, Tennessee high-voltage transformer manufacturing plant to Hyosung Heavy Industries for US$46.5M
recentDevelopments.read: The plant, opened in 2013, reopened under Hyosung in 2020 and has since been expanded repeatedly — so every current Memphis transformer expansion story belongs to Hyosung, not to Mitsubishi Electric.

relationships.note: MEPPI states it is developing 800 VDC power-delivery systems for next-generation AI factories through collaboration with NVIDIA, and NVIDIA also appears on Mitsubishi Electric's published UPS customer roster.
relationships.context:
The October 2025 MEPPI release is the only place in the public record where Mitsubishi Electric is placed inside the 800 VDC rack-power conversation. It matters because independent coverage of NVIDIA's 800 VDC ecosystem consistently names ABB, Hitachi Energy, Schneider Electric and Vertiv and does not name Mitsubishi Electric — so the relationship is visible first-party and invisible third-party.

The corporate strategy published in May 2026 corroborates the direction at board level, naming development of next-generation 800 V and 1,500 V DC power supply systems and a PUE 1.1 data center as targets. NVIDIA separately appears on the company's own customer roster, so the link is both a development collaboration and a supply relationship, though no order value or product has been disclosed.

relationships.note: Mitsubishi Power and Mitsubishi Electric jointly developed a next-generation gas turbine control system that completed functional testing in December 2025, with market launch targeted for fiscal 2026.
relationships.context:
These are two legally and operationally separate companies that share only the Mitsubishi keiretsu name — Mitsubishi Power is a brand of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (TSE: 7011), while Mitsubishi Electric is TSE: 6503. Neither is a subsidiary or affiliate of the other, and conflating them is the single most common error made about either company.

The control system is the one place in the public record where they build a product together: instrumentation and control from the electrical company, the machine from the heavy-industry one. Mitsubishi Power's DIASYS control series has more than 3,000 units delivered to over 60 countries, so the joint product enters an established installed base. Both companies published the announcement on the same day from their own newsrooms.

relationships.note: The two companies signed a memorandum of understanding in June 2021 to run a feasibility study on jointly developed high-voltage switching solutions with zero global-warming potential, beginning with a 245 kV dead-tank circuit breaker.
relationships.context:
This is a cooperation between two competitors in gas-insulated switchgear, aimed squarely at the regulation that threatens the product both of them sell: SF6 has a global warming potential the companies state as roughly 23,500 times that of carbon dioxide, and jurisdictions are moving to restrict it.

The two are simultaneously listed as competing majors in gas-insulated switchgear by Straits Research and Mordor Intelligence, and independent transformer rankings place Siemens Energy above Mitsubishi Electric. Cooperating on the technology that would obsolete the gas while competing on the equipment that uses it is the structure of the relationship, and no product from the MoU has been announced.

relationships.via: Lithium-ion battery strings for the 9900D UPS
relationships.note: Samsung SDI lithium-ion battery product specifications and installation manuals are published by Mitsubishi Electric as 9900D peripherals, and the company hosts a dedicated article on Samsung SDI lithium-ion battery safety.
relationships.context:
The 9900D is marketed as Lithium Ready, and Samsung SDI is the lithium cell partner whose documentation the company publishes alongside its own. The relationship is a component-supply one at the battery-string level rather than a joint development.

It sits alongside VRLA, VLA, NiCad and pure-lead options from Narada, EnerSys, Deka/East Penn and C&D Technologies, so lithium is one path among several rather than the default. That matters commercially: the battery is the part of a UPS that ages and needs replacing, and the choice of chemistry is a maintenance and fire-code decision as much as an energy-density one.

relationships.via: HRL-700 VRLA battery strings for the 9900D UPS
relationships.note: Narada HRL-700 data sheets and HRL series warranty documents are published by Mitsubishi Electric as approved 9900D battery options.
relationships.context:
Narada is one of five named battery suppliers whose documentation Mitsubishi Electric hosts for the 9900D, covering the high-rate VRLA option. The HRL-700 is a high-rate long-life lead-acid product of the type used where a UPS needs minutes rather than hours of autonomy.

The link is documented only through published product documentation rather than through any announced agreement, so its scale is unknown. It is nonetheless a real supply relationship: a UPS vendor publishes battery documentation for the strings it has qualified against its own charger and monitoring.

relationships.note: Tesla appears on Mitsubishi Electric's own published UPS customer roster.
relationships.context:
The roster is company-published structured data listing several hundred named UPS customers. It establishes the fact of a customer relationship and nothing more — no product, capacity, site or date is disclosed for any entry.

Read it as evidence of installed base rather than of a specific deployment. For a dossier the value is negative as well as positive: a vendor that publishes a customer list and does not publish a single data-center order value or reference capacity is telling you where its disclosure line sits.

relationships.note: Oracle appears on Mitsubishi Electric's own published UPS customer roster.
relationships.context:
As with the other roster entries, the company publishes the name without a product, site, capacity or date. Oracle is a hyperscale data-center operator, so the entry is more materially interesting than most, but it cannot be sized from any public source.

No Mitsubishi Electric release, case study or third-party report located in this research names a data-center UPS order, reference installation or deployed capacity for any hyperscaler. The published case studies are for Element Critical, Sabey, UScellular and Grupo Salinas.

relationships.note: QTS appears on Mitsubishi Electric's own published UPS customer roster.
relationships.context:
QTS is a hyperscale colocation landlord, so the entry places Mitsubishi Electric UPS inside a wholesale data-center estate. The roster also carries Sabey, CoreSite, CyrusOne, Flexential, TierPoint, Cologix, Serverfarm, Element Critical and Evocative among colocation operators.

As with every other roster entry, no capacity, site or date is published. The colocation cluster is nonetheless the clearest published evidence of where this UPS line actually sells.

relationships.note: Research and Markets names Mitsubishi Electric and Piller Power Systems together in the set of vendors it says dominate the data center UPS market for 2025-2030.
relationships.context:
This is the only source located in this research that names Piller and Mitsubishi Electric in one defined market. It is a title-level ranking rather than a share table, and no percentage is attached to either party.

The two compete from opposite ends of the technology: Piller's franchise is rotary and diesel-rotary UPS with a flywheel store, while Mitsubishi Electric's is large static UPS with a battery store. Where they meet is the same purchase decision at the same megawatt scale, which is why a market report lists them together and why a buyer comparing them is comparing architectures rather than products.

relationships.note: Named alongside Mitsubishi Electric in the Research and Markets dominant-vendor set for data center UPS, and again among the top companies in the power transformer market by MarketsandMarkets.
relationships.context:
Eaton meets Mitsubishi Electric in two of its three relevant markets — data-center UPS and transformers — and is one of the five suppliers Mordor Intelligence says control roughly 55-60% of the North America medium-voltage switchgear market, a tier Mitsubishi Electric sits below.

Neither firm publishes a Mitsubishi Electric share figure in any of these markets, so the comparison is positional rather than quantitative. Where research firms rank rather than list, Mitsubishi Electric is consistently in the named-major tier and consistently not in the leading five.

relationships.via: Data-center UPS and switchgear manufacturing capacity
relationships.note: Named alongside Mitsubishi Electric in the Research and Markets dominant-vendor set for data center UPS, and set directly against MEPPI on North American switchgear capital investment in Manufacturing Dive's coverage of the Pennsylvania plant.
relationships.context:
The two compete in data-center UPS, and the same trade article that reported MEPPI's $86M Pennsylvania switchgear factory noted Vertiv expanding switchgear and busbar manufacturing in the US and internationally — putting the two in the same capacity race.

Vertiv is also inside NVIDIA's publicly named 800 VDC collaboration set, with an 800 VDC portfolio release stated for the second half of 2026, while Mitsubishi Electric's 800 VDC work is visible only through its own release. On the rack-power architecture the two are at different points of public commitment.

relationships.note: Named alongside Mitsubishi Electric in the Research and Markets dominant-vendor set for data center UPS and in Straits Research's gas-insulated switchgear participant list.
relationships.context:
Global Market Insights puts Schneider Electric at 24.3% of the data-center UPS market in 2024 and the top five — Eaton, Schneider, Vertiv, ABB and Delta — at about 60% combined, with Mitsubishi Electric named in the top seven and given no percentage. That asymmetry is the relationship: a named major with no published share against a leader with one.

Mordor Intelligence also identifies Schneider's EcoStruxure Grid as part of a shift of competition toward software bundled with switchgear, which is the same direction Mitsubishi Electric's $1.4bn PCI Energy Solutions acquisition points.

relationships.note: Named alongside Mitsubishi Electric in the Research and Markets dominant-vendor set for data center UPS and among the gas-insulated switchgear majors by Straits Research.
relationships.context:
ABB meets Mitsubishi Electric in both UPS and gas-insulated switchgear, and is one of the five suppliers Mordor says control roughly 55-60% of North American medium-voltage switchgear.

ABB is also the first name in NVIDIA's publicly announced 800 VDC collaborations, and Mordor cites its 800 V DC lineup as trimming cooling loads 10-15% in hyperscale facilities. Both companies are therefore making the same architectural bet, with ABB's version far more visible in independent coverage.

relationships.note: Named alongside Mitsubishi Electric in the Research and Markets dominant-vendor set for data center UPS.
relationships.context:
Delta sits inside the top-five group Global Market Insights credits with about 60% of the data-center UPS market, where Mitsubishi Electric is named in the top seven without a share.

The two also approach the market from different scales: Delta's data-center franchise runs from rack power shelves upward, while Mitsubishi Electric's runs from the 80 kVA to 2 MW room-scale UPS downward. They meet in the middle of a hall rather than across a catalogue.

relationships.via: Gas-insulated switchgear and North American manufacturing capacity
relationships.note: Named among the gas-insulated switchgear majors alongside Mitsubishi Electric by Straits Research, and set directly against MEPPI's Pennsylvania plant in a head-to-head North American capital-investment comparison.
relationships.context:
The clearest quantitative comparison between the two comes from Manufacturing Dive's coverage of the Pennsylvania factory, which reported Mitsubishi Electric's $86M single-plant investment alongside Hitachi Energy's $155M across three North American plants, including $60M for its own Pennsylvania switchgear and breaker facility.

Against Hitachi Energy's stated $9bn global programme, Mitsubishi Electric's North American grid-equipment capital commitment is one to two orders of magnitude smaller. Hitachi Energy also leads or co-leads the transformer rankings that place Mitsubishi Electric outside the top five.

relationships.note: Named among the gas-insulated switchgear majors alongside Mitsubishi Electric by Straits Research and Mordor Intelligence, and among the top power-transformer companies by MarketsandMarkets.
relationships.context:
GE Vernova is one of the five suppliers Mordor Intelligence says control roughly 55-60% of the North America medium-voltage switchgear market, a tier Mitsubishi Electric sits below in the same report.

The two also meet in transformers, where MarketsandMarkets names both among the top companies while a competing ranking places Siemens Energy, Hitachi Energy, GE Grid Solutions, TBEA and CG Power in the top five and Mitsubishi Electric outside it.

relationships.note: Mordor Intelligence profiles Mitsubishi Electric Power Products and Powell Industries alongside each other in its North America medium-voltage switchgear company roster, and Straits Research lists both among gas-insulated switchgear participants.
relationships.context:
Both sit outside the five suppliers Mordor says control roughly 55-60% of the North American medium-voltage switchgear market, but they occupy that space differently. Powell's stated differentiator in the same report is speed from a domestic plant — tailored switchgear in ten weeks from Texas — while Mitsubishi Electric's is a vacuum and gas circuit-breaker portfolio to 800 kV backed by a new $86M Pennsylvania factory.

The overlap is real but partial: metal-clad switchgear, which is Powell's core product class, is not a named MEPPI product line, while gas-insulated switchgear at transmission voltages is not Powell's. They meet at the medium-voltage breaker rather than across the whole lineup.

policyExposure.exposure: The Bureau of Industry and Security added 407 new tariff codes to the Section 232 steel and aluminium derivative list effective for goods entered on or after 2025-08-18, applying a 50% tariff to the steel and aluminium content of covered products. Transformers and switchgear are within the derivative scope, and trade advisers report that the 2026 restructuring assesses duties on full customs value with a capped 15% rate for specified electrical-grid equipment through 2027-12-31, rising to 25% from 2028. Mitsubishi Electric names tariffs as a negative driver in its own FY2026 operating-profit bridge but does not separately quantify the impact.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company announced strengthened production facilities for its energy systems business in the US and Japan in October 2024, including an $86M advanced switchgear factory in the Pittsburgh region producing vacuum and gas circuit breakers, supported by a $4M Pennsylvania RACP grant and a $2.75M Pennsylvania First grant. It also states that its high-voltage circuit breakers are fully assembled and tested in the USA.

policyExposure.exposure: The company states that regulations to reduce or prohibit fluorinated gases in the electrical industry are being reviewed and implemented in various parts of the world, and puts SF6's global warming potential at roughly 23,500 times that of carbon dioxide. Gas-insulated switchgear and gas-insulated circuit breakers, which run from 145 kV to 800 kV in its catalogue, are the exposed product lines, and gas-insulated transformers use SF6 as their combined cooling and insulating medium.
policyExposure.mitigation: A stated SF6-free roadmap: a 72 kV vacuum circuit breaker with dry-air insulation as the current flagship, forthcoming vacuum models, an SF6 gas monitoring and analytics system, and a 2021 memorandum of understanding with Siemens Energy to study jointly developed zero-global-warming-potential high-voltage switching starting with a 245 kV dead-tank breaker.

policyExposure.exposure: The final rule took effect 2024-07-08 with compliance required on and after 2029-04-23. The exposure is indirect for Mitsubishi Electric: it sold its Memphis high-voltage transformer plant to Hyosung Heavy Industries in 2019 and announced a transfer of its distribution transformer business in April 2024, so the rule bears on its utility customers' procurement cycles rather than on its own US compliance obligations.
policyExposure.mitigation: No company statement on this rule was located.

policyExposure.exposure: ENERGY STAR is the only third-party efficiency benchmark Mitsubishi Electric cites in its own UPS literature, and it uses it as a positioning claim rather than treating it as a constraint: it states it holds the highest efficiency rating in the AC double-conversion category and that the SUMMIT Series sits at the top of all double-conversion UPS on the ENERGY STAR list. A published case study attributes substantial government rebates to the efficiency rating.
policyExposure.mitigation: Not applicable — the programme is used as a commercial advantage rather than mitigated.

policyExposure.exposure: The UPS line is listed to UL 1778 and CSA 22.2, meets IEC 62040-2 category C3 for electromagnetic compatibility and IEEE 587 / ANSI C62.41-1991 for surge withstand, and the 9900AEGIS carries an additional UL 924 listing at 80 and 100 kVA for emergency lighting. Collection gap: no IEC 62040-3 classification code is published for any model, so the standard classification that would let a specifier compare this line against a competitor's on a coded basis is absent from the public record.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company describes topology in words as true online double conversion, which is what the VFI classification denotes, and publishes full efficiency curves for that mode.

metrics.name: Earnings per share
metrics.expected: Investing.com and FT/Markit consensus ¥50.59; MarketBeat consensus US$0.6310 (GAAP, ADR)
metrics.result: The outlets disagree on the ACTUAL, not only the estimate: FT/Markit and Simply Wall St both carry ¥53.66 — matching the company's own reported basic EPS — while Investing.com carries ¥54.19. Simply Wall St labels its figure statutory and scores a 4.7% beat; Investing.com's basis is unlabelled and scores 7.1%; MarketBeat's GAAP ADR figure of $0.67 scores 6.2%. Analyst panel size also differs sharply: FT counts 16, Simply Wall St 14, and the ADR-only panel behind MarketBeat's aggregate rating is 3.

metrics.name: Adjusted operating profit
metrics.result: The adjusted figure is the one the company leads with. An independent analyst blog argues more than 60% of the ¥50.4bn adjusted increase is non-organic — roughly ¥22bn from a weaker yen and ¥9.05bn from a change of depreciation method from declining-balance to straight-line — putting organic growth nearer +20.6%. That is an attributed third-party calculation, not a company figure, and is carried here as attribution rather than fact.

metrics.name: Energy Systems orders
metrics.result: The single most striking operating number in the quarter, and the company attributes segment growth to North American transformer business expansion. Public Utility Systems orders were ¥153.8bn (+37%).

metrics.name: Net profit attributable to stockholders
metrics.result: Overseas revenue ratio 57% (+2pt). Full-year FY2027 guidance was raised on the print to ¥6,270.0bn revenue and ¥620.0bn adjusted operating profit, from ¥6,200.0bn and ¥590.0bn.

periods.commentary: The company labels this quarter Q1 FY2027; several trackers label the same period Q1 FY2026, so the period-end date is the only safe identifier. Guidance was raised on the print, with FX assumptions of ¥150/US$, ¥175/EUR and ¥21.5/CNY.

financials.commentary: Mitsubishi Electric reports in Japanese yen under IFRS with a fiscal year ending 31 March, and labels the year ending 31 March 2026 as FY2026. No normalized USD overlay is carried on any period. Converting these figures would require a citable fiscal-year average JPY/USD rate covering April 2025 to March 2026; the OECD quarterly series reachable in this research supplies the June, September and December 2025 quarters but not the March 2026 quarter, so any full-year average would be fabricated precision. The company's own guidance FX assumption of ¥150/US$ is a planning rate for a future year, not a conversion basis for reported results. The figures are therefore left in reported currency and kpiNorm is false. Two further honesty notes: no retrievable outlet published a pre-print full-year consensus for FY2025 or FY2026, so the annual verdicts above compare against the company's own guidance and say so; and for the latest quarter the outlets disagree on the reported EPS itself, not merely on the estimate, so each is carried with its outlet and basis named.

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that Mitsubishi Electric's exposure to the AI data-center build is real but concentrated in transmission and distribution rather than in the UPS line that its data-center marketing leads with. Basis: Energy Systems orders rose 80% year on year in the quarter ended 2026-06-30 and the company attributed segment growth to North American transformer business expansion, while Public Utility Systems — the sub-segment containing UPS — saw full-year FY2026 orders fall 9% even as its revenue rose 20%. The order book is being written on the grid side.

**(High confidence)** We assess the company is deliberately positioned against eco-mode as a competitive stance rather than lacking the capability. Basis: it publishes no eco-mode efficiency figure for any model, states plainly that silicon carbide makes eco-mode and its switching event unnecessary, and publishes 98.2% double-conversion efficiency on the SUMMIT Series. Where most of the industry buys back double-conversion losses by running the load on bypass and engineering a detection-and-transfer budget, this vendor is arguing the losses are now small enough not to. That is a coherent technical position and it is also a narrow one — it depends on the customer valuing the removed failure mode more than the remaining efficiency gap.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that vertical integration into its own power semiconductors is the company's most durable differentiator and its least legible one. Basis: it states it is the only UPS brand designing and manufacturing its own semiconductors, and that competitors may use older-generation Mitsubishi Electric IGBTs while only it uses current designs. The claim is unverifiable from outside and is never quantified, but it is consistent with the silicon-carbide product existing at all and with the company's semiconductor segment. Treat it as a credible structural advantage of unknown commercial weight.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess the $86M Pennsylvania switchgear factory is primarily a tariff and lead-time hedge rather than a growth investment. Basis: it was announced in October 2024 with $6.75M of Pennsylvania state grants, produces vacuum and gas circuit breakers transitioning to predominantly vacuum, and lands in the same period as the Section 232 derivative expansion that put transformers and switchgear inside a tariff regime assessed on full customs value. Against Hitachi Energy's $155M across three North American plants and its stated $9bn global programme, this is a defensive footprint rather than a bid for share.

**(Low confidence)** Trade press and market-research firms consistently name Mitsubishi Electric in the leading vendor set for data-center UPS, power transformers and gas-insulated switchgear, but no firm reachable in this research publishes a market-share percentage for it in any of those three markets, and where sources rank rather than list it falls below the top five in transformers and outside the top five in North American medium-voltage switchgear. We assess the company is a credible top-seven participant across all three and a share leader in none, but the evidence is a pattern of named-without-a-number rather than a measurement.

**Collection gap — the largest unresolved question in this dossier.** The company attributed Q1 FY2027 Energy Systems growth to North American transformer business expansion, yet it sold its only US transformer plant, in Memphis, Tennessee, to Hyosung Heavy Industries for $46.5M in 2019, announced a transfer of its distribution transformer business in April 2024, and its 2024 US capacity investment was for switchgear rather than transformers. No source located in this research identifies where that North American transformer capacity physically sits — whether it is import-and-service, Japan-supplied, or an unannounced facility.

**Collection gap — no named data-center UPS deployment exists anywhere in the public record.** The company publishes a customer roster naming NVIDIA, Tesla, Oracle, QTS, Sabey, CoreSite, CyrusOne, Flexential and several hundred others, and publishes case studies for Element Critical, Sabey, UScellular and Grupo Salinas. It publishes no order value, no reference capacity and no named hyperscaler deployment. A dossier reader should treat the roster as evidence of installed base and not as evidence of scale.

**Collection gap — the quality-misconduct record ends in October 2022 and its consequences are unsourced.** An external investigative committee reported 197 cases of improper quality control across all 22 Japanese sites, and the company admitted falsifying transformer test data over roughly four decades. That is the most consequential risk item for a dossier centred on transformers and switchgear. Whether it produced fines, customer claims, contract losses or ongoing monitoring is not established by any source located here, and the absence of later reporting is not evidence of resolution.
